figure4.title: Descending Control of Locomotor Activity by Modulation of Gain and Projectome

interpretation_1_total_external_input.description: Target neurons receive scheduled drive (15, 22, 30 pA), non-targets receive baseline background 10 pA
interpretation_1_total_external_input.outcome: Robust rhythmic bursting across all gaits, amplitude increases +112%, but bilateral alternation is preserved throughout (Walk=160.0Â°, Trot=162.3Â°, Bound=163.3Â°); no switch to bilateral synchrony

interpretation_2_additive_drive_over_bac.description: Scheduled drive is added to normal background (30 pA baseline + 15/22/30 pA -> 45/52/60 pA total input)
interpretation_2_additive_drive_over_bac.outcome: High drive pushes membrane potentials into upper saturation ceiling (Fmax = 50 Hz), causing loss of rhythmicity and tonic saturation (54.7% saturation) without producing bounding synchrony

figure4.discrepancy_diagnosis: Under the authors' released network connectivity and rate model equations: Walking and Trotting produce alternating traveling waves with burst amplitude increasing from Walk to Trot. However, under high descending drive and 5-HT gain modulation (Bounding), the network maintains bilateral reciprocal alternation (~163°) rather than switching to bilateral synchrony (~0°). Arbitrary visual scaling and forced synchrony have been removed; genuine computational outcome is reported.
